detail.longDescription: I have following script on my server (in user panel) javascript triggers XMLHttpRequest to php: var setting_product_updates document.getElementById('receive_product_updates_email').change = function(e){ //peevent checkbox check if working! if(setting_product_updates)return false; setting_product_updates = true; var receive_product_updates_email = e.target.checked ? '1' : '0'; var url = 'product_management.php'; var xhr = new XMLHttpRequest; xhr.onreadystatechange = function() { if (this.readyState === 4){ if (this.status === 200) { setting_product_updates = false; } } } xhr.onerror = function() { setting_product_updates = false; } xhr.open("POST", url, true); xhr.setRequestHeader("Content-Type", "application/x-www-form-urlencoded"); var user_id = userLicencesTable.getAttribute('data-user-id') var params = '' + 'update_receive_product_updates=1' + 'receive_product_updates_email=' + receive_product_updates_email + '&user_id=' + user_id xhr.send(params); } php: if (isset($_POST['update_receive_product_updates']) && isset($_POST['user_id']) ) { // connect to the database $db = mysqli_connect(DB_HOST, DB_USER, DB_PASSWORD, DB_NAME); $user_id = $_POST['user_id']; $receive_product_updates_email = trim($_POST['receive_product_updates_email']); $query = "UPDATE users SET receive_product_updates_email='$receive_product_updates_email' WHERE id=?"; $stmt = $db->prepare($query); $stmt->bind_param("s", $user_id); $stmt->execute(); echo json_encode('1'); } My question: If XMLHttpRequest can be faked with fake parameters, how can I make sure user does not abuse this?
